title: Bauschinger effect of linear kinematic hardening: tension, then back to zero strain
source: J2 plasticity with Prager's linear kinematic hardening in uniaxial stress (W. Prager, Ing.-Arch. 1955; Simo and Hughes, Computational Inelasticity, Springer 1998, §2.3): from σ_a = σ_y + E_t (ε_a − σ_y/E) the material unloads elastically by 2σ_y and then hardens with E_t, so at zero strain σ = σ_a − 2σ_y − E_t (ε_a − 2σ_y/E)

quantities.quantity: axial stress back at zero strain after a pull to ε_a = 0.01
quantities.reason: a homogeneous small-strain state the element represents exactly, with increments that end at the load path's turn; isotropic hardening would give −281.835 (it yields again only at −σ_a)
(σ_a − σ_y)/H forward plus E/(E + H) (ε_a − 2σ_y/E) in reverse
